Physical inspection. Trace Lift Sender A through the selected conduit and the 10 m workshop patch lead to Workshop Receiver B. The service-loop conduit is 95 m (105 m total); the direct conduit is 85 m (95 m total). These are the supplied T02/T01 lengths in the fictional PROFILE-COPPER-100, whose inclusive limit is 100 m. Record the selected path and measured result at the current configuration and attempt. Valid inspection recorded means the inspection was performed, even when length exceeds the profile. It does not mean the link or a service works. A changed path leaves the old result stale until a new inspection. Source: labeled training conduit and inspection kit in The Arrival Lift; PHY04; T01/T02.

evidence.text: Prism Vault readings use the fictional optical exercise: transmit −3 dBm, sensitivity −14 dBm, maximum receive −1 dBm and required reserve 2 dB. Passive path A has total loss 8 dB: receive −11 dBm and reserve 3 dB. Path B has loss 9 dB: receive −12 dBm and reserve exactly 2 dB. Both matched, inspected paths pass the inclusive bounds. At 10 dB loss, −13 dBm is above sensitivity but its 1 dB reserve fails. A separately observed 0 dBm receive fails the −1 dBm overload bound. Repeat the measurement after changing the selected path or starting a new attempt.

Carry the compatibility and inspection record from Photon Gardens into this measurement. An incompatible selected optic/fiber pair is incorrect even if arithmetic would pass. Missing units, unknown profiles, negative passive loss, or simultaneously asserting 0 dBm receive from −3 dBm transmit through nonnegative passive loss are a problem with the supplied exercise, not a learner failure.

alternatives.label: Validate passive optical path B
alternatives.explanation: With matching optics and fresh measurements, 9 dB loss yields −12 dBm and exactly 2 dB reserve. This inclusive boundary is as valid as path A; no preferred-answer penalty applies.

This fictional budget is 30 W delivered at the endpoint boundary after losses. Compatible kit A demands 12 W + 11 W = 23 W, leaving 7 W. Kit B demands 12 W + 11 W + 7 W = 30 W, leaving zero. Both fit the inclusive budget when each port constraint also passes. The 12 W + 11 W + 10 W proposal totals 33 W and exceeds it by 3 W. Do not subtract unspecified line losses a second time.

Both toy endpoints negotiate. A advertises 1000/full and 100/full; B advertises 100/full and 10/half. The only common member is 100/full. The rates are decimal megabits per second; neither endpoint gains unsupported modes.

alternatives.label: Validate compatible kit B

evidence.text: Clockworks supplies ordered sample positions 0,1,2,3 and toy levels −3,+1,+3,−1. The declared linear map is −3→00, −1→01, +1→10, +3→11. Decoding gives 00|10|11|01 = 00101101: eight represented bits in four symbols. Pause, step, replay or use the notebook; no timing score is required. If the exercise omits a sample position or supplies an undefined symbol, its instructions need correction; it is not your mistake.

The Metronome illustrates agreed physical sampling positions, not NTP or IP/MAC address discovery. The common 100/full selection must occur in both supplied advertised sets; matching alone does not discover addresses. The highlighted NQ payload (4E 51; 01001110 01010001) sits inside an opaque upper-interface frame, not a complete two-byte Ethernet frame.
